cars.variant: Italia Ford-351 coupe — 1972 build, AutoWeek 1984 drive reference
cars.specification_market: Original Intermeccanica Torino/Italia road-development family, conservatively grouping related Griffith and Omega stages, selected 1972 Ford-351 coupe borrowed from Automarque in Arlington for John Matras's AutoWeek article dated 2 April 1984 and later republished by the author. Eleven attributes use that exact firsthand account; they are not universal factory-originality claims. Keep Ford 351 as the writer's engine designation, without assuming Cleveland/Windsor, exact cc, horsepower, induction specification or gearbox type/count from a T-handle shifter. The separate 289-powered quarter-mile/top-speed reference, generic mass, height and gearing are omitted. Body/chassis and suspension origins remain author-reported, not independently authenticated components. Manufacturer history supports rename relationships only. Earlier licensed coupe photo is representative and does not authenticate model year, reference engine, chassis or originality. Dedicated racers, prototypes, replicas and additional body/engine versions are not admitted. Earlier Apollo and later Indra remain distinct research subjects, not extra admissions here.
cars.summary: The Italia is a distinctive Italian-American sporting hybrid: a bespoke steel-bodied, tube-frame road coupe combining Ford V8 power with four-wheel disc brakes. Its original road-drive coverage and manufacturer history establish its place in the transatlantic sports-car tradition. Count the Griffith/Omega/Torino/Italia development family once; renamed stages, different engines, bodies and individual chassis do not create additional records.

sources.source_type: Original firsthand road-drive article republished by its author
sources.notes: Complete relevant road-drive/history text read. Site structured author metadata names John Matras; https://rememberroad.com/about/ explains his own article reprints and Escape Road drives. Original magazine facsimile not read. Writer explicitly identifies the borrowed Automarque Arlington car as built in 1972 with Ford 351; all eleven attributes are scoped to that account. No Cleveland/Windsor identification, exact displacement conversion, output, gearbox type/count, torque, weight or dimensions inferred. Earlier 289-powered timed results are not transferred to this 351 reference. Fiat-truck suspension provenance and chassis description remain author-reported, not independent component authentication. Disputed designer attribution and production totals omitted.
